captive_summary: No public design study exists yet. No source describes any on-site power generation, backup gensets, or captive plant for the terminal.
confirmed_how: Da Nang city government's investment call (nhandan.vn, en.vneconomy.vn) describes the Lien Chieu 'bến cảng lỏng, khí' (liquid/gas port terminal) purely as LNG/LPG storage and distribution infrastructure seeking a private investor; no technical design (and hence no captive-power detail) has been published because no investor has yet been selected.
gogpt_prior_assessment: No GOGPT plant given (gogpt_prior=no). A separate 'Hoa Ninh LNG power plant' project exists ~10km away tied to the Hoa Ninh Industrial Park and PDP8, but it is a distinct project with no confirmed fuel-supply link to this terminal yet (no investor/pipeline design published for either side) — not this terminal's captive power in any case, since it would be an off-site utility plant, not on-site generation.
gogpt_candidate_basis: No on-site generation identified; terminal is a pre-investor storage/distribution proposal with no technical design published.
status_or_other_findings: Da Nang has requested the Hoa Ninh LNG power plant (separate project, ~10km from this terminal site, part of Hoa Ninh Industrial Park) be included in PDP8; no confirmed pipeline link between the two projects has been published.
notes: Too early-stage for a captive-power finding either way; revisit once an investor/EIA is published. No PowerPlantsSupplied relationship confirmed to any specific plant at this time — Hoa Ninh is a candidate but unconfirmed.

captive_summary: No captive gas power at the terminal. Gas flows FROM the terminal TO the power plant (PowerPlantsSupplied), not the reverse; no source describes any separate on-site generation for the terminal's own auxiliary load.
confirmed_how: Vietnam government e-newspaper (baochinhphu.vn) reports investment approval and Phase-1 groundbreaking (Jan 15, 2022) for the 'Hải Lăng LNG Power Center,' 1,500 MW / ~VND54,000bn, developed by T&T Group with Korean partners Hanwha, KOSPO and KOGAS — a single integrated LNG-to-power complex in which the terminal exists solely to fuel the plant.

verification_log.note: confirms Phase 1 capacity and investment figure

gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT's 'Hai Lang power station' (3,000 MW, gogpt_captive=False, 0.01 km away) IS the plant this terminal exists to supply — it is a merchant/utility combined-cycle power station selling to the grid, not this terminal's captive power (the direction is opposite: terminal feeds plant). gogpt_candidate_basis: GOGPT already tracks 'Hai Lang power station' at this site (gogpt_prior=yes); it is not a captive plant to add, and no separate on-site captive generator was found.
status_or_other_findings: Phase 1 targeted for commercial operation by Dec 31, 2029 per baochinhphu.vn; investors: KOGAS 20%, KOSPO 20%, Hanwha Energy 20%, T&T Group 40% (matches GEM owner field).

gogpt_candidate_basis: GOGPT already tracks 'Haiphong LNG power station' at this site; not a captive plant, and no separate on-site captive generator for the FSRU itself was found.

captive_summary: Screened: cancelled and never built. No subsequent public reporting (2021-2026) shows the project receiving formal investment approval, entering PDP8, breaking ground, or advancing in any way; GEM's own tracking already carries the terminal as cancelled. The Van Phong area subsequently saw other, unrelated developers (Petrolimex, Vingroup, Sumitomo) propose different LNG/power projects on nearby land — none tied to Millennium Energy — consistent with the original proposal having lapsed.

gogpt_candidate_basis: Project never advanced past a 2020 proposal announcement; no captive or merchant plant was ever built.
status_or_other_findings: None beyond the screen finding above.
